signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: JPY 1W average outperformance of +1.915% across 7 pairs versus SEK 1W average decline of -1.460% across 2 pairs generates an extreme 3.375% G10 spread that anchors JPY leadership into the Asia open. Weekend confirmation of BoJ preparation for a 1.25% policy rate amplifies divergence against the Riksbank's neutral stance (1.75% policy rate) and negative SEK ESI (-6.7). The Tokyo session open and Sweden CPI release on Monday resolve whether SEK underperformance extends. Trade bias: Bullish JPY/SEK into the open as monetary tightening divergence widens the performance spread. Catalyst: Sweden CPI release at 06:00 UTC and the upcoming 18 Sep BoJ rate decision. Risk: Sweden CPI prints significantly above the 0.4% y/y forecast, triggering an immediate SEK short squeeze.
evidence: G10 spread: 3.375%
SEK ESI at -6.7 vs JPY ESI at +23.8
BoJ next meeting: 18 Sep | SEK next meeting: 24 Sep

signals.title: AUD/USD — CROWDED LONG UNWIND RISK
signals.text: AUD COT Leveraged Funds net long of +48.4k sits at the 93rd percentile of 52-week positioning (z=+1.72), creating elevated crowded-long liquidation risk after AUD/USD closed Friday at 0.7173. Fed holds at 3.75%. The upcoming FOMC meeting on 16 Sep is the catalyst determining whether the US yield surge forces spec liquidation. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD on rallies as stretched speculative longs face US rate repricing headwinds. Catalyst: FOMC policy decision on 16 Sep followed by RBA meeting on 29 Sep. Risk: Break and hold above 0.7220 if broader risk appetite rebounds or commodities extend gains.

signals.title: USD/CHF — FED HIKE BETS VS REAL YIELD DIVERGENCE
signals.text: CHF COT Leveraged Funds net short of -14.0k at the 12th percentile (z=-1.09) and an extreme retail short skew of 97% on crosses like AUD/CHF leave the franc exposed as USD/CHF broke above 0.8150 to close at 0.8161. An expansive SOFR-over-SARON carry spread of +366bp and a wide US-Swiss real policy rate divergence (+1.35% USD vs -1.24% CHF) provide fundamental fuel for USD/CHF appreciation despite Middle East war rhetoric. The FOMC interest rate decision on 16 Sep is the catalyst that validates this upward trajectory. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CHF into the session open supported by widening nominal and real carry advantage. Catalyst: FOMC rate decision on 16 Sep ahead of SNB rate decision on 24 Sep. Risk: Reversal below 0.8074 (SMA20) if geopolitical safe-haven CHF inflows overwhelm the yield gap.

signals.title: EUR/USD — CARRY DISADVANTAGE & BEAR FLATTENER
signals.text: EUR Leveraged Funds net short of -46.4k holds firm as EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1601, hemmed in below its 20-day and 200-day moving averages (1.1630 and 1.1637). The US bear-flattener curve regime (+41.5bp 2s10s) and a +143bp OIS carry advantage for USD (SOFR 3.62% vs €STR 2.19%) sustain downward pressure on the pair despite the ECB's nominal hiking bias. Speeches from ECB Executive Board Member Schnabel and President Lagarde on Monday provide the next directional test. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD into early European trade while spot remains capped below 1.1635. Catalyst: ECB Schnabel speech at 09:15 UTC and Lagarde speeches starting 15:15 UTC ahead of 16 Sep FOMC. Risk: Daily close above 1.1640 invalidates the immediate bearish setup.
